summary: Redwood AE/SE team walked Lumina through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and a cost breakdown tied to their expected token mix and QPS. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated; security and data residency are blockers. Agreed next steps: pricing worksheet, security docs, POC kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood Inference. We have Priya our SE and Jordan from CSM with me.
[00:08] Sara Lopez: Hi all, Sara here from Lumina Health, thanks. We have Mark, Aisha, and Tom on our side.
[00:15] Alex Kim: Great, quick agenda - console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then we will go over a cost breakdown using your token profile. We'll leave time for Q&A and security. Sound good?
[00:28] Mark Chen: Yep, that's what we signed up for. We're mostly trying to figure out cost predictability and whether dedicated capacity makes sense.
[00:35] Priya Patel: Awesome. I'll share my screen - can you see the Redwood Console? (small pause) Sorry, is the window visible?
[00:45] Tom Rivera: We can see it, looks good.
[00:50] Priya Patel: Cool. Starting at the top, this is the Usage Analytics landing - overall tokens, successful requests, error rates. You can filter by time, model, or route. Notice the spike here - that was a canary test we ran last week, shows how latency changed under concurrency.
[01:10] Sara Lopez: The spike view is nice. Can you break down by route? We have a 'clinical-summary' route that is heavy on context length.
[01:18] Priya Patel: Yep, click into Per-route dashboards, pick your route, then you get throughput, p95/p99 latency, failures, and importantly token distribution per call. We also surface KV cache hit rates and prefix reuse.
[01:34] Mark Chen: KV cache - so that's the prefix caching for similar prompts? How configurable is that?
[01:39] Priya Patel: It's automatic by default but you can tune cache TTL and pin prefixes. For Dedicated customers we expose more controls. Also shows batching efficiency and how many requests were coalesced.
[01:52] Jordan Lee: One thing customers like is the per-route cost attribution. You can see token cost, batching gains, and effective cost per request.
[02:02] Aisha Rahman: Say more about the cost model - we need to show security and cost to exec.
[02:08] Priya Patel: Sure. Under Cost Insights we map model selection, quantization profile, and observed batching to a projected per-token cost. For example, this route uses a 4k context model at q4_0 quant which reduces GPU memory and cost by about 30% versus fp16 in many workloads.
[02:27] Sara Lopez: Is that empirical data from Redwood runs or theoretical?
[02:31] Priya Patel: It's a mix - baseline kernel timings are measured on our fleet, and then we apply workload-specific factors from historical requests. It's conservative but reflects real gains we've seen with similar customers.
[02:43] Mark Chen: Do you let us plug in our own token distribution? Our prompts are long, average 600 tokens in, 300 out.
[02:50] Priya Patel: Yes - you can upload a sample trace or give us a CSV and we'll profile it. We can run a 'what-if' using your traces and show Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparisons and expected latency percentiles.
[03:03] Tom Rivera: How do you show dedicated vs hosted?
[03:06] Priya Patel: There's a toggle - Dedicated will show reserved GPU pricing, predictable throughput graphs, and autoscale headroom. Hosted shows spot/rise capacity mix with slightly higher variance but no contract. We also overlay SLO attainment probabilities.
[03:20] Sara Lopez: Our SREs worry about fallbacks when capacity is constrained. What does Redwood do?
[03:25] Alex Kim: We have smart routing and automated fallback policies; if a primary model is constrained we'll route to an equivalent model variant or fall back to a smaller model gracefully. For enterprise customers we can configure canary and A/B rollouts.
[03:38] Aisha Rahman: From a security perspective we need audit logs, KMS, and SOC2. Do you have those features in Console?
[03:46] Jordan Lee: Yes - Console exposes audit trails for every API call, role-based access controls, and integrations with customer KMS for key wrapping. We are SOC2 Type II; we can share the report under NDA.
[03:58] Aisha Rahman: Good. Also need data residency options - on-prem or VPC?
[04:03] Alex Kim: We offer Redwood Private with VPC or on-prem deployments. For the demo today we're focused on hosted console behavior but we can map these dashboards to Private instances as well.
[04:16] Mark Chen: Back to cost - can you show a sample breakdown per route?
[04:20] Priya Patel: Sure, selecting clinical-summary route: here is token cost, model cost (GPU time), batching savings, cache savings, and the net per-call cost. You can expand and see the assumptions - model throughput numbers, tokenization overhead, and quantization profile.
[04:36] Sara Lopez: The per-call cost column is helpful. Can you export this for our finance team?
[04:41] Priya Patel: Yep export CSV or connect to the billing API for programmatic pulls.
[04:47] Tom Rivera: Any integrations for observability - Sentry, Datadog?
[04:51] Priya Patel: We have tracing hooks and can forward metrics to Datadog, Prometheus, and put spans into your tracing system. Also per-request token level traces for debugging.
[05:02] Aisha Rahman: A thought - when you show quantization savings, is there a quality estimate? We can't degrade output accuracy for clinical summaries.
[05:10] Priya Patel: Great question. We pair quantization recommendations with evals on held-out prompts; Console will surface a quality delta and confidence intervals. For high-risk routes we recommend keeping fp16 and using Dedicated cache optimizations instead.
[05:26] Sara Lopez: That sounds promising. What's the typical uplift from KV caching for repeated patient prompts?
[05:31] Priya Patel: It depends on reuse patterns; some customers see 20-60% token and latency reduction on routes with high prefix reuse.
[05:40] Mark Chen: So next steps, we'd like Redwood to run a sample cost model with our traces and give a Dedicated vs Hosted recommendation.
[05:47] Alex Kim: Absolutely - Priya can take your CSV. Also we'll send pricing and a dedicated capacity worksheet.
[05:53] Aisha Rahman: We'll also send our security questionnaire.
[05:56] Jordan Lee: I'll follow up with the SOC2 and compliance pack under NDA.
[06:01] Sara Lopez: Timeline - we hope to decide within two to three weeks, run a short POC if numbers look good.
[06:07] Alex Kim: Sounds good. Anything else?
[06:10] Tom Rivera: One quick ask - can the console show expected p95 under burst traffic for dedicated?
[06:15] Priya Patel: Yes, under the capacity planning tab we simulate burst scenarios and show SLA attainment with autoscale headroom.
[06:23] Sara Lopez: Great, thanks everyone.
[06:25] Alex Kim: Thanks folks - recap: we'll send pricing and security docs, Priya will run a cost model with your traces, Jordan will share SOC2. We'll aim to kick off POC next week.
[06:37] Mark Chen: Thanks, bye.
[06:39] (call ends)
